norms.heading: Procedure and venue.

path.label: Title XXX DOMESTIC RELATIONS
Chapter 452 Dissolution of Marriage, Divorce, Alimony and Separate Maintenance

norms.text:
1. The rules of the supreme court and other applicable court rules shall govern all proceedings pursuant to sections 452.300 to 452.415.

2. A proceeding for dissolution of marriage, legal separation, or declaration of invalidity of marriage shall be entitled: "In re the Marriage of ______ and ______".

3. The initial pleading in an original proceeding pursuant to sections 452.300 to 452.415 shall be denominated a "petition" and the responsive pleading in an original proceeding shall be denominated an "answer". Other pleadings in an original proceeding and all pleadings in other proceedings pursuant to sections 452.300 to 452.415 shall be denominated as provided in the rules of the supreme court and other applicable court rules.

4. Any party who files the initial pleading in an original proceeding pursuant to sections 452.300 to 452.415 shall be denominated the "petitioner" and any party who is required to file or who files a responsive pleading in an original proceeding shall be denominated the "respondent". Each party shall retain such denomination from the original proceeding in any other proceedings pursuant to sections 452.300 to 452.415.

5. An original proceeding pursuant to sections 452.300 to 452.415 shall be commenced in the county in which the petitioner resides or in the county in which the respondent resides. If an original proceeding is commenced in the county in which the petitioner resides, upon motion by the respondent filed prior to the filing of a responsive pleading, the court in which the proceeding is commenced may transfer the proceeding to the county in which the respondent resides if:

(1) The county in which the respondent resides had been the county in which the children resided during the ninety days immediately preceding the commencement of the proceeding; or

(2) The best interest of the children will be served if the proceeding is transferred to the county in which the respondent resides because:

(a) The children and at least one parent have a significant connection with the county; and

(b) There is substantial evidence concerning the present or future care, protection and personal relationships of the children in the county.

6. In proceedings pursuant to sections 452.300 to 452.415, "judgment" shall include a "decree".

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1070 fixe les règles de compétence territoriale du juge aux affaires familiales selon la résidence de la famille, des parents ou des enfants, avec des règles spéciales pour les demandes conjointes et alimentaires. Le § 5 de RSMo 452.300 règle le lieu des procédures matrimoniales et certains transferts liés aux enfants, tandis que RSMo 508.010 énonce les règles générales de venue.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1070 establishes family-court venue based on the residence of the family, parents, or children, with special rules for joint and support claims. RSMo 452.300(5) governs venue and certain child-related transfers in marriage proceedings, while RSMo 508.010 supplies general civil venue rules; neither matches the full French scheme.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une requête unique des époux. Le Missouri prévoit en principe une petition initiale et un respondent, mais RSMo 452.320 envisage que les deux époux déclarent sous serment que le mariage est irrémédiablement rompu.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires one joint petition by both spouses. Missouri generally structures the case around a petition and respondent, although RSMo 452.320 recognizes a sworn statement by both parties that the marriage is irretrievably broken.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1107 fixe les modes d’introduction du divorce et le contenu obligatoire de l’acte, notamment la date d’audience et certaines interdictions relatives au fondement et aux faits. Les dispositions du Missouri prévoient une petition, son contenu, sa dénomination et les conditions de commencement, mais selon des exigences différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1107 regulates how divorce is commenced and specifies mandatory contents, including a hearing date and restrictions on stating the legal basis and facts. Missouri provides for a petition, its required contents and commencement requirements, but with materially different conditions.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 This is the same as Rule 3 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article soumet la procédure de séparation de corps aux règles de la procédure de divorce. Le RSMo 452.300 prévoit que les règles judiciaires régissent l’ensemble des procédures de dissolution et de séparation légale.
correspondences.note_en: The article subjects legal-separation proceedings to the rules governing divorce proceedings. RSMo 452.300 provides that court rules govern all dissolution and legal-separation proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1131 soumet la conversion à la procédure écrite ordinaire et exclut les demandes reconventionnelles, sauf sur les conséquences du divorce. L’article 452.360(3) prévoit la conversion de la séparation en dissolution sur motion, tandis que l’article 452.300 renvoie aux règles de procédure applicables, sans reprendre la restriction relative aux demandes reconventionnelles.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1131 requires ordinary written procedure for conversion and bars counterclaims except those concerning the consequences of divorce. Section 452.360(3) provides for conversion by motion, while §452.300 incorporates applicable procedural rules but does not address the counterclaim limitation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la procédure écrite ordinaire devant le tribunal judiciaire, la publicité des débats et du jugement, et soumet une demande particulière de prorogation à cette procédure. La Rule 55.29 prévoit l’audience publique, tandis que le RSMo 452.300 encadre globalement la procédure matrimoniale, sans reproduire ces règles.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires ordinary written procedure, public hearings and judgment, and places a specific family-home request within that procedure. Rule 55.29 addresses open-court trials, while RSMo 452.300 generally governs matrimonial proceedings, but neither reproduces the full French rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article fixe la compétence territoriale et organise l'introduction de la demande en séparation judiciaire de biens, avec des mesures de publicité au répertoire civil et dans la presse. Le RSMo 452.300 règle le lieu et la forme d'une procédure de séparation légale, mais ne prévoit ni la séparation de biens ni ces publicités matrimoniales.
correspondences.note_en: The article fixes venue and governs commencement of a judicial separation-of-property proceeding, including civil-register and newspaper publicity. RSMo 452.300 governs venue and pleading form for legal-separation proceedings, but not separation of property or these matrimonial-publicity measures.

norms.heading: Judgment of dissolution, grounds for — legal separation, when — pregnancy status not to prevent judgment — judgments to contain Social Security numbers.

path.label: Title XXX DOMESTIC RELATIONS
Chapter 452 Dissolution of Marriage, Divorce, Alimony and Separate Maintenance

norms.text:
1. The court shall enter a judgment of dissolution of marriage if:

(1) The court finds that one of the parties has been a resident of this state, or is a member of the armed services who has been stationed in this state, for ninety days immediately preceding the commencement of the proceeding and that thirty days have elapsed since the filing of the petition; and

(2) The court finds that there remains no reasonable likelihood that the marriage can be preserved and that therefore the marriage is irretrievably broken; and

(3) To the extent it has jurisdiction, the court has considered and made provision for child custody, the support of each child, the maintenance of either spouse and the disposition of property.

2. The court shall enter a judgment of legal separation if:

(1) The court finds that one of the parties has been a resident of this state, or is a member of the armed services who has been stationed in this state, for ninety days immediately preceding the commencement of the proceeding and that thirty days have elapsed since the filing of the petition; and

(2) The court finds that there remains a reasonable likelihood that the marriage can be preserved and that therefore the marriage is not irretrievably broken; and

(3) To the extent it has jurisdiction, the court has considered and made provision for the custody and the support of each child, the maintenance of either spouse and the disposition of property.

3. Pregnancy status shall not prevent the court from entering a judgment of dissolution of marriage or legal separation.

4. Any judgment of dissolution of marriage or legal separation shall include the last four digits of the Social Security numbers of the parties. The full Social Security number of each party and each child shall be retained in the manner required under section 509.520.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge vérifie la recevabilité, le consentement libre et éclairé, peut faire modifier la convention avec l’accord des parties et homologue celle-ci en prononçant immédiatement le divorce. Le § 452.325 RSMo prévoit le contrôle du caractère déraisonnable de l’accord, sa révision éventuelle et son intégration au jugement ; les §§ 452.305 et 452.320 encadrent le jugement de dissolution et l’audience.
correspondences.note_en: The judge verifies admissibility and informed consent, may modify the agreement with the parties’ consent, and immediately approves it and grants the divorce. RSMo 452.325 provides review for unconscionability, possible revision, and incorporation into the decree; RSMo 452.305 and 452.320 govern the dissolution judgment and hearing.

correspondences.note_fr: Le divorce est prononcé par le juge aux affaires familiales sur le seul fondement de l’acceptation des époux. L’article 452.320 permet la dissolution lorsque les parties déclarent que le mariage est irrémédiablement rompu, mais exige une audience et une constatation judiciaire; l’article 452.305 ajoute les conditions générales de résidence et de règlement des conséquences du divorce.
correspondences.note_en: The court grants divorce solely on the spouses’ acceptance. RSMo 452.320 permits dissolution when the parties state that the marriage is irretrievably broken, but requires a hearing and judicial finding; RSMo 452.305 additionally imposes general residency and ancillary-relief requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article interdit de statuer sur le principe du divorce avant l'expiration d'un délai d'un an dans le cas visé. RSMo 452.320 prévoit certains délais de séparation de douze ou vingt-quatre mois, tandis que RSMo 452.305 impose seulement trente jours après le dépôt : les règles sont donc seulement partielles et différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article postpones judgment on the principle of divorce until a one-year period has expired in the specified case. RSMo 452.320 provides twelve- or twenty-four-month separation periods in certain contested cases, while RSMo 452.305 requires only thirty days after filing; the comparison is therefore partial.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux deux époux de demander expressément et conjointement que le juge n’énonce pas leurs torts et griefs dans les motifs, celui-ci constatant seulement les faits constitutifs d’une cause de divorce. Les §§ 452.320 et 452.305 imposent une constatation judiciaire du caractère irrémédiablement rompu du mariage et, le cas échéant, de faits justificatifs, sans prévoir cette dispense conjointe ; la Rule 73.01 concerne plus généralement les motifs et constatations du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows both spouses expressly and jointly to ask the judge not to state their faults and grievances in the reasoning, limiting the decision to finding facts constituting grounds for divorce. Sections 452.320 and 452.305 require findings that the marriage is irretrievably broken and, where applicable, supporting facts, but provide no comparable joint waiver; Rule 73.01 addresses opinions and factual findings more generally.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article interdit le jugement avant l'expiration d'un mois suivant la publicité de la demande. Le RSMo 452.305(2) exige également l'écoulement de trente jours depuis le dépôt de la demande avant un jugement de séparation légale, mais dans un cadre différent et avec des conditions supplémentaires.
correspondences.note_en: The article bars judgment until one month after the application has been publicized. RSMo 452.305(2) likewise requires thirty days to elapse after filing before a legal-separation judgment, but applies to a different proceeding and includes additional conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque seules une pension alimentaire ou une contribution aux charges du mariage sont demandées, le juge doit inviter les parties à s’expliquer sur la prestation compensatoire avant de prononcer le divorce. Le Missouri règle la maintenance et les demandes de soutien, mais ne prévoit pas cette obligation procédurale spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: If only maintenance or contributions to marital expenses are sought, the French judge must invite submissions on a compensatory award before granting divorce. Missouri addresses maintenance and requested relief, but does not impose this specific invitation or compensatory-award procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: La demande française doit reposer sur un seul cas de divorce, les demandes subsidiaires et la substitution d’un cas à un autre étant en principe irrecevables. La Rule 55.10 autorise au contraire les demandes alternatives, tandis que les articles 452.310 et 452.320 organisent les allégations et constatations relatives aux causes de dissolution.
correspondences.note_en: The French rule requires a divorce claim to rely on one ground and generally bars alternative claims or switching grounds during the proceeding. Rule 55.10 expressly permits alternative and even inconsistent claims, while §§ 452.310 and 452.320 address allegations and findings concerning dissolution grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article énumère des mentions obligatoires et exige la date ainsi que les signatures des deux époux et de leur avocat. RSMo 452.310 impose la vérification et certaines mentions ; RSMo 452.312 impose des identifiants et renseignements sur les employeurs ; Rule 55.03 et RSMo 509.030 régissent la signature et les déclarations.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies mandatory contents and requires dating and signatures by both spouses and their lawyer. RSMo 452.310 requires verification and specified information; RSMo 452.312 requires identifying and employer information; Rule 55.03 and RSMo 509.030 govern signatures and declarations.

correspondences.note_fr: La saisine résulte de la remise de la requête, suivie de l’audition éventuelle du mineur et de la convocation personnelle des époux avant leur audition. Les §§ 452.310 et 452.320 RSMo organisent la requête, le service et l’audience de dissolution ; le § 452.785 permet au tribunal d’ordonner la comparution personnelle d’une partie ou d’un enfant, mais dans un cadre différent.
correspondences.note_en: The court is seized by filing the petition, followed by any child hearing and personal notice to the spouses before their hearing. RSMo 452.310 and 452.320 address the petition, service, and dissolution hearing; RSMo 452.785 permits compelled personal appearance of a party or child, but in a different framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1107 fixe les modes d’introduction du divorce et le contenu obligatoire de l’acte, notamment la date d’audience et certaines interdictions relatives au fondement et aux faits. Les dispositions du Missouri prévoient une petition, son contenu, sa dénomination et les conditions de commencement, mais selon des exigences différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1107 regulates how divorce is commenced and specifies mandatory contents, including a hearing date and restrictions on stating the legal basis and facts. Missouri provides for a petition, its required contents and commencement requirements, but with materially different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1132 impose, en cas de séparation consensuelle et d’audition d’un mineur, une requête détaillée, une convention sur les conséquences du divorce et les signatures des époux et avocats. Le Missouri prévoit la conversion sur motion et encadre les conventions de séparation, mais n’exige pas ces mêmes mentions, circonstances ni signatures conjointes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1132 requires, when a minor seeks to be heard, a detailed conversion petition, a divorce-consequences agreement, and signatures by both spouses and counsel. Missouri provides conversion by motion and regulates separation agreements, but does not impose the same particulars, triggering condition, or joint-signature requirements.

norms.text:
1. Every petition for dissolution of marriage or legal separation, every motion for modification of a decree respecting maintenance or support, and every petition or motion for support of a minor child shall contain the last four digits of the Social Security number of the petitioner or movant, if a person, and the last four digits of the Social Security number of the respondent. The name and address of the petitioner's and respondent's current employer shall be provided and retained in the same manner as required under section 509.520.

2. Every responsive pleading to a petition for dissolution of marriage or legal separation, motion for modification of a decree respecting maintenance or support, and petition or motion for support of a minor child shall contain the name and address of the current employer and the last four digits of the Social Security number of the respondent, if the respondent is a person.

3. Every decree dissolving a marriage, every order modifying a previous decree of dissolution or divorce, and every order for support of a minor child shall contain the last four digits of the Social Security numbers of the parties, if disclosed by the pleadings.

4. The full Social Security number of each party and each child shall be retained in the manner required by section 509.520.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article énumère des mentions obligatoires et exige la date ainsi que les signatures des deux époux et de leur avocat. RSMo 452.310 impose la vérification et certaines mentions ; RSMo 452.312 impose des identifiants et renseignements sur les employeurs ; Rule 55.03 et RSMo 509.030 régissent la signature et les déclarations.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies mandatory contents and requires dating and signatures by both spouses and their lawyer. RSMo 452.310 requires verification and specified information; RSMo 452.312 requires identifying and employer information; Rule 55.03 and RSMo 509.030 govern signatures and declarations.

norms.heading: Authorized motions — restraining order, when, answer, when due, effect of — child support, temporary order, when, amount.

path.label: Title XXX DOMESTIC RELATIONS
Chapter 452 Dissolution of Marriage, Divorce, Alimony and Separate Maintenance

norms.text:
1. In a proceeding for dissolution of marriage or legal separation, either party may move for temporary maintenance and for temporary support for each child entitled to support. The motion shall be accompanied by an affidavit setting forth the factual basis for the motion and the amounts requested. In a proceeding for disposition of property, maintenance or support following the dissolution of the marriage by a court which lacked personal jurisdiction over the absent spouse, either party may move for maintenance and for support of each child entitled to support. This motion shall be accompanied by an affidavit setting forth the factual basis for the motion and the amounts requested. This motion and the affidavit shall be served as though an original pleading upon the opposite party.

2. As a part of a motion for temporary maintenance or support or by independent motion accompanied by affidavit, either party may request the court to issue an order after notice and hearing:

(1) Restraining any person from transferring, encumbering, concealing, or in any way disposing of any property except in the usual course of business or for the necessities of life and, if so restrained, requiring the person to notify the moving party of any proposed extraordinary expenditures and to account to the court for all extraordinary expenditures made after the order is issued;

(2) Enjoining a party from harassing, abusing, molesting or disturbing the peace of the other party or of any child;

(3) Excluding a party from the family home or from the home of the other party upon a showing that physical or emotional harm would otherwise result;

(4) Establishing and ordering compliance with a custody order and providing for the support of each child.

3. The court may issue a restraining order only if it finds on the evidence that irreparable injury would result to the moving party if an order is not issued until the time for answering has elapsed.

4. An answer may be filed within ten days after service of notice of motion or at the time specified in the restraining order.

5. On the basis of the showing made and in conformity with section 452.335 on maintenance and section 452.340 on support, the court may issue a temporary injunction and an order for temporary maintenance or support in such amounts and on such terms as are just and proper in the circumstances.

6. A restraining order or temporary injunction:

(1) Does not prejudice the rights of the parties or the child which are to be adjudicated at subsequent hearings in the proceedings;

(2) May be revoked or modified prior to final judgment on a showing by affidavit of the facts necessary to revocation or modification of a final judgment pursuant to section 452.370; and

(3) Terminates when the final judgment is entered or when the petition for dissolution or legal separation is voluntarily dismissed.

7. The court shall enter a temporary order requiring the provision of child support pending the final judicial determination if there is clear and convincing evidence establishing a presumption of paternity pursuant to section 210.822. In determining the amount of child support, the court shall consider the factors set forth in section 452.340.

8. Any order entered in modification or vacation of any temporary order entered pursuant to this section may be retroactive to the date of entry of the original temporary order.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge aux affaires familiales peut cumuler les fonctions de juge de la mise en état et de juge des référés, et statuer selon une procédure accélérée au fond. Le Missouri prévoit des mesures temporaires en matière familiale et l’accélération de certaines affaires de placement, d’adoption ou de déchéance des droits parentaux, sans instituer les mêmes fonctions juridictionnelles.
correspondences.note_en: The family judge may act as case-management and emergency-relief judge and use an expedited merits procedure. Missouri provides temporary family-law orders and expedited handling for specified child-protection, placement, termination, or adoption cases, but does not create the same combined judicial role.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1075-1 exige une déclaration sur l’honneur lorsque la prestation compensatoire est demandée ou prévue par convention. Le Missouri prévoit un affidavit pour les demandes de maintenance temporaire et encadre la maintenance selon les ressources et besoins, mais n’impose pas une déclaration patrimoniale équivalente pour toute demande.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1075-1 requires a sworn financial declaration when compensatory support is sought or provided for by agreement. Missouri requires an affidavit for temporary maintenance motions and evaluates maintenance by financial factors, but does not require the same general declaration.

correspondences.note_fr: Le Missouri évalue les ressources et actifs pour la maintenance et permet, par discovery, d’obtenir les documents pertinents. Il ne prévoit toutefois pas ici une demande judiciaire ciblée imposant les déclarations fiscales, justificatifs de charges ou pièces patrimoniales visés par l’article 1075-2.
correspondences.note_en: Missouri considers financial resources and assets in maintenance proceedings and permits discovery of relevant documents. These texts do not establish a targeted judicial mechanism requiring the tax returns, expense records, or asset documents described in Article 1075-2.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1109 organise une saisine urgente permettant une assignation à bref délai en divorce, avec mesures provisoires, délais de remise et contrôle du temps laissé à la défense. Le RSMo 452.315 prévoit des mesures temporaires et une audience sur motion, tandis que la Rule 55.30 permet d’avancer l’audition, sans reprendre toute cette procédure d’urgence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1109 creates an expedited divorce procedure with temporary measures, filing deadlines, and a safeguard ensuring sufficient preparation time for the defense. RSMo 452.315 provides temporary relief and notice-based hearings, while Rule 55.30 permits expedited hearings, but neither reproduces the full procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1117 organise la saisine et l'audience relatives aux mesures provisoires du divorce, notamment la maintenance, le soutien des enfants, la garde et certaines mesures de protection, ainsi que la prise en compte d'accords. Les §§ 452.315 et 452.380 couvrent plusieurs mesures temporaires, tandis que le § 452.325 concerne les accords de séparation. Les textes fournis ne précisent pas la participation des avocats ni la date d'effet des mesures.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1117 governs the filing and hearing of divorce-related provisional measures, including maintenance, child support, custody, protective relief, and consideration of agreements. Sections 452.315 and 452.380 cover several temporary measures, while § 452.325 concerns separation agreements. The supplied texts do not specify attorney participation or the effective date of measures.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1118 permet, en cas de fait nouveau et avant le dessaisissement de la juridiction, de supprimer, modifier ou compléter les mesures provisoires. Le § 452.315(6) autorise la révocation ou la modification d'une ordonnance restrictive ou d'une injonction temporaire avant le jugement définitif, mais ne reprend pas expressément la condition de fait nouveau ni la possibilité de compléter les mesures.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1118 permits provisional measures to be vacated, modified, or supplemented after a new fact arises and before the court is divested. Section 452.315(6) permits revocation or modification of a restraining order or temporary injunction before final judgment, but does not expressly include the new-fact condition or supplementation of measures.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article règle la continuation des mesures de protection pendant une procédure de divorce ou de séparation, leur remplacement éventuel par les mesures provisoires du divorce et le transfert des demandes au juge du divorce. Le Missouri prévoit la fin de certaines mesures lors d'un jugement de dissolution ou de séparation, tout en traitant les procédures de protection comme indépendantes, avec des effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs continuation of protective measures during divorce or legal-separation proceedings, their possible replacement by temporary divorce measures, and transfer of related motions to the divorce court. Missouri provides for termination of certain protective-order provisions upon dissolution or legal separation and treats protection proceedings as independent, producing different effects.

norms.heading: Finding that marriage is irretrievably broken, when — notice — denial by a party, effect of — alternate findings.

path.label: Title XXX DOMESTIC RELATIONS
Chapter 452 Dissolution of Marriage, Divorce, Alimony and Separate Maintenance

revisor_notes: (1976) This act is not a true "no fault" dissolution law and dissolution should not be granted over the objection of an innocent spouse. In re Marriage of Mitchell (A.), 545 S.W.2d 313.

(1977) If a party denies under oath that a marriage is irretrievably broken the court must find one of the statutory grounds has been met. Failure to prove any of these grounds must result in a refusal to dissolve the marriage. In re Marriage of Capstick (A.), 547 S.W.2d 522.
(1977) Held, parties had been living "separate and apart" even though they lived in the same home. In re Marriage of Uhls (A.), 549 S.W.2d 107.
(1977) Failure to mail notice does not deprive the court of jurisdiction. LeBeau v. LeBeau (A.), 556 S.W.2d 204.

(1977) Court erroneously applied the law by failing to hold a hearing on whether marriage is irretrievably broken, when absent party, after receiving notice of interlocutory finding, files an objection within ten days. Brown v. Brown (A.), 561 S.W.2d 374.
(1978) Court must make specific finding that marriage was irretrievably broken before granting a decree of dissolution, B.W. v. F.E.W. (A.), 562 S.W.2d 137.

correspondences.note_fr: La demande française doit reposer sur un seul cas de divorce, les demandes subsidiaires et la substitution d’un cas à un autre étant en principe irrecevables. La Rule 55.10 autorise au contraire les demandes alternatives, tandis que les articles 452.310 et 452.320 organisent les allégations et constatations relatives aux causes de dissolution.
correspondences.note_en: The French rule requires a divorce claim to rely on one ground and generally bars alternative claims or switching grounds during the proceeding. Rule 55.10 expressly permits alternative and even inconsistent claims, while §§ 452.310 and 452.320 address allegations and findings concerning dissolution grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une requête unique des époux. Le Missouri prévoit en principe une petition initiale et un respondent, mais RSMo 452.320 envisage que les deux époux déclarent sous serment que le mariage est irrémédiablement rompu.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires one joint petition by both spouses. Missouri generally structures the case around a petition and respondent, although RSMo 452.320 recognizes a sworn statement by both parties that the marriage is irretrievably broken.

correspondences.note_fr: La saisine résulte de la remise de la requête, suivie de l’audition éventuelle du mineur et de la convocation personnelle des époux avant leur audition. Les §§ 452.310 et 452.320 RSMo organisent la requête, le service et l’audience de dissolution ; le § 452.785 permet au tribunal d’ordonner la comparution personnelle d’une partie ou d’un enfant, mais dans un cadre différent.
correspondences.note_en: The court is seized by filing the petition, followed by any child hearing and personal notice to the spouses before their hearing. RSMo 452.310 and 452.320 address the petition, service, and dissolution hearing; RSMo 452.785 permits compelled personal appearance of a party or child, but in a different framework.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge vérifie la recevabilité, le consentement libre et éclairé, peut faire modifier la convention avec l’accord des parties et homologue celle-ci en prononçant immédiatement le divorce. Le § 452.325 RSMo prévoit le contrôle du caractère déraisonnable de l’accord, sa révision éventuelle et son intégration au jugement ; les §§ 452.305 et 452.320 encadrent le jugement de dissolution et l’audience.
correspondences.note_en: The judge verifies admissibility and informed consent, may modify the agreement with the parties’ consent, and immediately approves it and grants the divorce. RSMo 452.325 provides review for unconscionability, possible revision, and incorporation into the decree; RSMo 452.305 and 452.320 govern the dissolution judgment and hearing.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’acceptation expresse et concordante du principe de la rupture, par procès-verbal ou déclaration annexée aux conclusions, avec des mentions obligatoires à peine de nullité. L’article 452.320 prévoit plutôt les déclarations sous serment relatives au caractère irrémédiablement rompu du mariage et la procédure de vérification judiciaire; l’article 452.310 impose la vérification de la requête et de la réponse.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs express, concordant acceptance of the principle of marital breakdown through a court record or attached declaration, with mandatory wording on pain of nullity. RSMo 452.320 instead addresses sworn statements that the marriage is irretrievably broken and judicial findings, while RSMo 452.310 requires verified pleadings.

correspondences.note_fr: Le divorce est prononcé par le juge aux affaires familiales sur le seul fondement de l’acceptation des époux. L’article 452.320 permet la dissolution lorsque les parties déclarent que le mariage est irrémédiablement rompu, mais exige une audience et une constatation judiciaire; l’article 452.305 ajoute les conditions générales de résidence et de règlement des conséquences du divorce.
correspondences.note_en: The court grants divorce solely on the spouses’ acceptance. RSMo 452.320 permits dissolution when the parties state that the marriage is irretrievably broken, but requires a hearing and judicial finding; RSMo 452.305 additionally imposes general residency and ancillary-relief requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article interdit de statuer sur le principe du divorce avant l'expiration d'un délai d'un an dans le cas visé. RSMo 452.320 prévoit certains délais de séparation de douze ou vingt-quatre mois, tandis que RSMo 452.305 impose seulement trente jours après le dépôt : les règles sont donc seulement partielles et différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article postpones judgment on the principle of divorce until a one-year period has expired in the specified case. RSMo 452.320 provides twelve- or twenty-four-month separation periods in certain contested cases, while RSMo 452.305 requires only thirty days after filing; the comparison is therefore partial.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux deux époux de demander expressément et conjointement que le juge n’énonce pas leurs torts et griefs dans les motifs, celui-ci constatant seulement les faits constitutifs d’une cause de divorce. Les §§ 452.320 et 452.305 imposent une constatation judiciaire du caractère irrémédiablement rompu du mariage et, le cas échéant, de faits justificatifs, sans prévoir cette dispense conjointe ; la Rule 73.01 concerne plus généralement les motifs et constatations du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows both spouses expressly and jointly to ask the judge not to state their faults and grievances in the reasoning, limiting the decision to finding facts constituting grounds for divorce. Sections 452.320 and 452.305 require findings that the marriage is irretrievably broken and, where applicable, supporting facts, but provide no comparable joint waiver; Rule 73.01 addresses opinions and factual findings more generally.

norms.heading: Separation agreements authorized, effect of — orders for disposition of property, when — terms of agreement, how enforced.

path.label: Title XXX DOMESTIC RELATIONS
Chapter 452 Dissolution of Marriage, Divorce, Alimony and Separate Maintenance

norms.text:
1. To promote the amicable settlement of disputes between the parties to a marriage attendant upon their separation or the dissolution of their marriage, the parties may enter into a written separation agreement containing provisions for the maintenance of either of them, the disposition of any property owned by either of them, and the custody, support and visitation of their children.

2. In a proceeding for dissolution of marriage or for legal separation, the terms of the separation agreement, except terms providing for the custody, support, and visitation of children, are binding upon the court unless it finds, after considering the economic circumstances of the parties and any other relevant evidence produced by the parties, on their own motion or on request of the court, that the separation agreement is unconscionable.

3. If the court finds the separation agreement unconscionable, the court may request the parties to submit a revised separation agreement or the court may make orders for the disposition of property, support, and maintenance in accordance with the provisions of sections 452.330, 452.335 and 452.340.

4. If the court finds that the separation agreement is not unconscionable as to support, maintenance, and property:

(1) Unless the separation agreement provides to the contrary, its terms shall be set forth in the decree of dissolution or legal separation and the parties shall be ordered to perform them; or

(2) If the separation agreement provides that its terms shall not be set forth in the decree, only those terms concerning child support, custody and visitation shall be set forth in the decree, and the decree shall state that the court has found the remaining terms not unconscionable.

5. Terms of the agreement set forth in the decree are enforceable by all remedies available for the enforcement of a judgment, and the court may punish any party who willfully violates its decree to the same extent as is provided by law for contempt of the court in any other suit or proceeding cognizable by the court.

6. Except for terms concerning the support, custody or visitation of children, the decree may expressly preclude or limit modification of terms set forth in the decree if the separation agreement so provides.
revisor_notes: Effective 1-01-74

(1979) Purpose of statute to put to rest questions of overreaching and fraud in the settlement of property questions, does not require the trial court to make evidentiary examinations of the economic circumstances only after it is found that the separation agreement is unconscionable. Block v. Block (A.), 593 S.W.2d 584.

(1987) This section allows but does not require court to investigate and examine the economic circumstances of the parties to the divorce and other relevant factors in determining conscionability of the settlement agreements. Dow v. Dow, 732 S.W.2d 906 (Mo. banc).

(1989) Amendment to statute which changes the age on which the obligation to pay child support terminates is a change in condition which authorizes a modification of the judgment where father did not agree to anything beyond that required by law. (Mo.App.W.D.) Kocherov v. Kocherov, 775 S.W.2d 539.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 12 impose au juge d’appliquer le droit, de restituer leur exacte qualification aux faits et actes, tout en prévoyant certaines limites conventionnelles et la possibilité de statuer comme amiable compositeur. La Rule 70.02 concerne la soumission au jury du droit applicable, tandis que le RSMo 452.325 rend certains accords matrimoniaux contraignants pour le tribunal, sans reprendre le régime général de l’article 12.
correspondences.note_en: Article 12 requires the judge to apply the governing law and assign the correct legal characterization to facts and acts, subject to limited party agreements and possible amicable-composition authority. Rule 70.02 addresses submission of applicable law to the jury, while RSMo 452.325 binds the court to certain marital agreements, without reproducing the article’s general rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 281 prévoit qu’en cas de conciliation pendant l’expertise, l’expert constate que sa mission est devenue sans objet et en informe le juge; les parties peuvent demander que leur accord reçoive force exécutoire. La Rule 88.08 organise un accord écrit issu d’une médiation et son exécution, tandis que les deux sections RSMo prévoient, dans des contextes particuliers, l’approbation ou l’exécution judiciaire d’un règlement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 281 provides that, when the parties settle during the expert process, the expert reports that the mission has become moot; the parties may ask the judge to make their agreement enforceable. Rule 88.08 governs a written mediation settlement and its enforcement, while the two RSMo sections provide court approval or judgment enforcement of settlements in specialized contexts.

correspondences.note_fr: La requête doit être accompagnée, le cas échéant, d’une convention complète réglant les effets du divorce, notamment la liquidation du régime matrimonial, ainsi que du formulaire de l’enfant. Le § 452.325 RSMo reconnaît les accords écrits de séparation et leur intégration ou leur contrôle par le tribunal, mais ne reprend pas les mêmes annexes ni l’exigence notariale française.
correspondences.note_en: The petition must include, where applicable, a comprehensive agreement governing the divorce, including property liquidation, and the child’s hearing form. RSMo 452.325 recognizes written separation agreements and their incorporation or review by the court, but does not require the same attachments or French notarial form.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge vérifie la recevabilité, le consentement libre et éclairé, peut faire modifier la convention avec l’accord des parties et homologue celle-ci en prononçant immédiatement le divorce. Le § 452.325 RSMo prévoit le contrôle du caractère déraisonnable de l’accord, sa révision éventuelle et son intégration au jugement ; les §§ 452.305 et 452.320 encadrent le jugement de dissolution et l’audience.
correspondences.note_en: The judge verifies admissibility and informed consent, may modify the agreement with the parties’ consent, and immediately approves it and grants the divorce. RSMo 452.325 provides review for unconscionability, possible revision, and incorporation into the decree; RSMo 452.305 and 452.320 govern the dissolution judgment and hearing.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut refuser l’homologation d’une convention insuffisante, demander une convention révisée et prendre des mesures concernant les enfants ou les époux. RSMo 452.325 prévoit également le contrôle judiciaire d’une convention de séparation et la possibilité d’en demander la révision, mais sans le délai de six mois ni le mécanisme précis d’ajournement prévus par le CPC.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may refuse to approve an inadequate agreement, request a revised agreement, and make orders concerning the children or either spouse. RSMo 452.325 likewise provides judicial review of a separation agreement and permits a revised agreement, but it lacks the CPC’s six-month deadline and specific adjournment mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1117 organise la saisine et l'audience relatives aux mesures provisoires du divorce, notamment la maintenance, le soutien des enfants, la garde et certaines mesures de protection, ainsi que la prise en compte d'accords. Les §§ 452.315 et 452.380 couvrent plusieurs mesures temporaires, tandis que le § 452.325 concerne les accords de séparation. Les textes fournis ne précisent pas la participation des avocats ni la date d'effet des mesures.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1117 governs the filing and hearing of divorce-related provisional measures, including maintenance, child support, custody, protective relief, and consideration of agreements. Sections 452.315 and 452.380 cover several temporary measures, while § 452.325 concerns separation agreements. The supplied texts do not specify attorney participation or the effective date of measures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1132 impose, en cas de séparation consensuelle et d’audition d’un mineur, une requête détaillée, une convention sur les conséquences du divorce et les signatures des époux et avocats. Le Missouri prévoit la conversion sur motion et encadre les conventions de séparation, mais n’exige pas ces mêmes mentions, circonstances ni signatures conjointes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1132 requires, when a minor seeks to be heard, a detailed conversion petition, a divorce-consequences agreement, and signatures by both spouses and counsel. Missouri provides conversion by motion and regulates separation agreements, but does not impose the same particulars, triggering condition, or joint-signature requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1133 organise l’examen judiciaire et l’homologation de la convention, avec possibilité de modification dans le mois et refus motivé en cas de difficulté. L’article 452.325 permet au juge d’examiner la convention, de demander une convention révisée et de l’intégrer au jugement, mais ne reprend pas la procédure française ni l’obligation de mentionner le délai d’appel.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1133 governs judicial review and approval of the agreement, including resubmission within one month and refusal if difficulties remain. Section 452.325 permits review and revision of a separation agreement and its inclusion in the decree, but does not reproduce the French procedure or required appeal-deadline statement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1143 organise l’homologation judiciaire d’une convention parentale : requête conjointe, absence de modification par le juge, décision sans débat en principe et appel du refus selon la procédure gracieuse. Le RSMo 452.325 encadre le contrôle et l’intégration des accords de séparation, mais dans une procédure et avec des effets différents; la Rule 55.30 permet une décision sans audience orale.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1143 governs judicial approval of a parental agreement: joint application, no judicial modification, normally no hearing, and appeal of refusal under noncontentious procedure. RSMo 452.325 regulates court review and incorporation of separation agreements but in a different proceeding and with different effects; Rule 55.30 permits decisions without oral argument.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose que la convention précise la valeur des biens ou droits attribués au titre de la prestation compensatoire et exige un acte authentique notarié pour les immeubles. Le Missouri encadre les accords de séparation et le partage des biens, ainsi que l’enregistrement des décisions affectant un immeuble, mais ne prévoit pas ces exigences notariales spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the agreement to state the value of property or rights awarded as compensatory relief and requires an authentic notarial instrument for real estate. Missouri regulates separation agreements and property division, and permits recording decrees affecting real estate, but does not impose these specific notarial requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article étend les dispositions du chapitre aux séparations de corps conclues par acte sous signature privée contresigné par avocats et déposé chez un notaire. Le RSMo 452.325 traite des conventions écrites de séparation et de leur effet dans une procédure judiciaire de séparation, sans prévoir cette forme extrajudiciaire ni le dépôt notarial.
correspondences.note_en: The article extends the chapter’s provisions to legal separations concluded by privately signed instruments countersigned by attorneys and deposited with a notary. RSMo 452.325 addresses written separation agreements and their effect in judicial legal-separation proceedings, but does not provide for this out-of-court form or notarial deposit.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose le régime général de l’accord amiable : formation par échange des consentements, écrit et éventuelle force exécutoire. La Rule 88.08 et les RSMo 452.325 et 511.740-511.750 prévoient des accords écrits ou des soumissions et leur exécution, mais dans des cadres plus spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes a general regime for amicable agreements: formation by consent, possible written form, and enforceability. Rule 88.08 and RSMo 452.325 and 511.740-511.750 address written settlements or submissions and enforcement, but only in more specific settings.

correspondences.note_fr: Le texte français exige une information du mineur sur son droit d’être entendu et assisté, à peine d’impossibilité d’homologation ou d’apposition de la formule exécutoire. Les textes du Missouri prévoient une représentation procédurale du mineur, l’examen de l’intérêt des enfants en médiation et l’approbation d’accords familiaux, sans imposer ces mêmes conditions.
correspondences.note_en: The French provision requires notice of the minor’s rights to be heard and assisted, barring approval or enforcement-form attachment if omitted. Missouri provisions address minor representation, children’s best interests in mediation, and approval of family agreements, but do not impose the same conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC français subordonne l’homologation à la licéité et à l’ordre public et interdit toute modification. Le Missouri encadre séparément certains accords familiaux : il peut demander une convention révisée ou rendre ses propres ordonnances, et approuver ou modifier un accord de contact post-adoption selon l’intérêt de l’enfant.
correspondences.note_en: French procedure requires an agreement to be lawful and consistent with public policy and forbids judicial modification. Missouri separately regulates certain family agreements: it may request a revised agreement or issue its own orders, and may approve or modify a post-adoption contact agreement according to the child’s best interests.

(1975) Rights acquired under a contract to purchase land constitute "property" and "marital property" and are subject to division by the court in a dissolution of marriage. Claunch v. Claunch (A.), 525 S.W.2d 788.

(1976) All property acquired subsequent to marriage taken in joint names is marital property subject to division upon dissolution unless (1) it is shown that such property was acquired in exchange for property acquired prior to the marriage, and (2) it is shown by clear and convincing evidence that the transfer was not intended as a provision for a settlement upon or as a gift to the other spouse. Conrad v. Bowers (A.), 533 S.W.2d 614.

(1976) For the purposes of this division of marital property under this section, the "conduct" of the parties during the marriage is a relevant factor to be considered by the trial court and the award to the husband of all of the real estate determined to be marital property was not error. Conrad v. Bowers (A.), 533 S.W.2d 614.
(1976) Trial courts are vested with broad discretion in dividing marital property in dissolution of marriage proceedings. In re Marriage of Vanet (A.), 544 S.W.2d 236.
(1976) The word "conduct" means general conduct of the parties during the marriage and is not limited to conduct relating to financial misdeeds. Butcher v. Butcher (A.), 544 S.W.2d 249.
(1976) For discussion of division of marital property and definition of same see Davis v. Davis (A.), 544 S.W.2d 259.

(1977) While wife's misconduct was to be taken into account in dividing marital property, it had begun late in the nineteen year marriage and was not such as to deprive her of right to share equitably in marital property. Thus, in addition to shares in closely held corporation awarded by trial court, she would be awarded a farm acquired by parties during marriage. Marriage of Schulte (A.), 546 S.W.2d 41.

(1977) Requirement that court make a division of marital property in a dissolution action is mandatory and failure to comply results in no final judgment in the action. The fact that a final judgment has not been rendered bars an appeal under the provisions of § 512.020, RSMo. Corder v. Corder (A.), 546 S.W.2d 798.

(1977) Property purchased with earnings during marriage is marital property regardless of how title is taken. Held error to set a future date for sale of property and allow a party a dollar value when sold. Inflation could seriously alter the value of the amount received so that proper judgment should have been for a percentage of the sale to be held in the future. Ortmann v. Ortmann (A.), 550 S.W.2d 226.
(1977) Held, failure of either party's petition to ask for division of property does not relieve trial judge from duty to make a division of the property. Hulsey v. Hulsey, (A.), 550 S.W.2d 902.

(1977) A husband may not voluntarily limit his work to reduce his income and escape support payments. A court may in proper circumstances impute an income to a husband according to what he could have earned by the use of his best efforts. Klinge v. Klinge (A.), 554 S.W.2d 474.
(1978) Statute does not require equal division of marital property, but only "just" division. This is true where one spouse has engaged in marital misconduct. Arp v. Arp (A.),572 S.W.2d 232.
(1978) Personal jurisdiction over an absent spouse is not necessary to confer jurisdiction for the purpose of dividing marital property. Chenoweth v. Chenoweth (A.), 575 S.W.2d 871.

(1984) "Source of funds" theory, adopted in this case, requires that the court determine the character of property by the source of funds financing the purchase, so that the property is considered to have been "acquired" as it is paid for. This theory allows for reimbursement for increase in value of the property. Hoffman v. Hoffman (Mo. banc), 676 S.W.2d 817.
(1985) Held, the "source of funds rule" as announced in Hoffman v. Hoffman, 676 S.W.2d 817 (Mo banc 1984) should be retrospectively applied. Sumners v. Sumners, (Mo.), 701 S.W.2d 720.

(1987) Goodwill in a professional practice is property subject to division pursuant to this section and is defined as the value of the practice which exceeds its tangible assets and which is the result of the tendency of clients/patients to return to and recommend the practice irrespective of the reputation of the individual practitioner. Hanson v. Hanson, 738 S.W.2d 429 (Mo. banc.).
(1987) Proper date for valuing marital property in a dissolution proceeding is the date of the trial. Taylor v. Taylor, 736 S.W.2d 388 (Mo. banc.).

(1987) It was proper for the court to consider, as an economic circumstance, in making a division of property, the sums voluntarily expended by husband for the support and education of a healthy adult child and to offset the wife's entitlement to husband's retirement pay by sums she received or would have received in maintenance. In Re Marriage of Dildy, 737 S.W.2d 756 (Mo.App.S.D.).
(1997) Statute does not allow the court to quash a QDRO and replace it with a domestic relations order that was not qualified. Offield v. Offield, 955 S.W.2d 247 (Mo.App.W.D.).
(1999) Statute does not give a trial court discretion to divide and distribute marital property to the parties' children. Randolph v. Randolph, 8 S.W.3d 160 (Mo.App.W.D.).

(2003) Section is more specific concerning authorization for modifying qualified domestic relations order and thus prevails over more general statute precluding modification of marital property division. Ricketts v. Ricketts, 113 S.W.3d 255 (Mo.App.W.D.).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1080 impose de préciser la valeur des biens ou droits attribués à titre de prestation compensatoire et, pour les immeubles, les mentions nécessaires à la publicité foncière. RSMo 452.330(6) permet l’enregistrement d’un jugement affectant le titre immobilier, tandis que la Rule 74.07 permet de transférer judiciairement le titre; ces textes n’imposent pas la même indication de valeur.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1080 requires the value of property or rights awarded as compensatory payment to be stated and, for real property, requires the particulars needed for recording. RSMo 452.330(6) permits recording a decree affecting title to real estate, and Rule 74.07 permits judicial vesting of title, but neither requires the same statement of value.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article rend applicables les règles procédurales du partage et attribue au juge familial les procédures d’apposition de scellés et d’état descriptif. Les Rules 96.01, 96.08 et 96.32 organisent le partage de biens réels ou personnels; le RSMo 452.330 règle la division des biens matrimoniaux, mais aucun texte ne prévoit les scellés et l’état descriptif.
correspondences.note_en: The article applies partition procedures and assigns the family judge authority over sealing and inventory proceedings. Rules 96.01, 96.08, and 96.32 govern partition of real or personal property, while RSMo 452.330 governs marital-property division; none addresses sealing and inventory specifically.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose que la convention précise la valeur des biens ou droits attribués au titre de la prestation compensatoire et exige un acte authentique notarié pour les immeubles. Le Missouri encadre les accords de séparation et le partage des biens, ainsi que l’enregistrement des décisions affectant un immeuble, mais ne prévoit pas ces exigences notariales spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the agreement to state the value of property or rights awarded as compensatory relief and requires an authentic notarial instrument for real estate. Missouri regulates separation agreements and property division, and permits recording decrees affecting real estate, but does not impose these specific notarial requirements.

revisor_notes: (1975) For extensive discussion of the law under this section, see In re Marriage of Powers (A.), 527 S.W.2d 949.
(1976) This section does not apply to modification of existing dissolution decree but only to original decree. Modifications are governed by § 453.370. Sifers v. Sifers (A.), 544 S.W.2d 269.
(1976) For discussion of "abuse of discretion" and items to be considered in making property settlements, support and attorney's fee awards, see Beckman v. Beckman (A.), 545 S.W.2d 300.
(1977) Held, trial court erred in making a periodically decreasing or "stairstepped" award. Modifications must not be made on speculation. In re Marriage of Cornell (A.), 550 S.W.2d 823.

(1977) Appellate court held that under the circumstances wife, though guilty of misconduct, was entitled to greater proportion of marital property and a continuation, after dissolution of marriage, of maintenance of $375.00 a month awarded by trial court. Marriage of Schulte (A.), 546 S.W.2d 41.

(1977) Held, "reasonable needs" does not automatically equal the standard of living established during the marriage. There is an affirmative duty on the part of a spouse seeking dissolution to seek employment. Brueggemenn v. Bureggemann (A.), 551 S.W.2d 853.
(1977) Maintenance in gross may be awarded under this section. Miller v. Miller (A.), 553 S.W.2d 482.

(1977) Statute allowing award of maintenance in gross was not repealed by the dissolution of marriage statutes and § 452.335 does not preclude award of maintenance in gross. Carr v. Carr (A.), 556 S.W.2d 511.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1075-1 exige une déclaration sur l’honneur lorsque la prestation compensatoire est demandée ou prévue par convention. Le Missouri prévoit un affidavit pour les demandes de maintenance temporaire et encadre la maintenance selon les ressources et besoins, mais n’impose pas une déclaration patrimoniale équivalente pour toute demande.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1075-1 requires a sworn financial declaration when compensatory support is sought or provided for by agreement. Missouri requires an affidavit for temporary maintenance motions and evaluates maintenance by financial factors, but does not require the same general declaration.

correspondences.note_fr: Le Missouri évalue les ressources et actifs pour la maintenance et permet, par discovery, d’obtenir les documents pertinents. Il ne prévoit toutefois pas ici une demande judiciaire ciblée imposant les déclarations fiscales, justificatifs de charges ou pièces patrimoniales visés par l’article 1075-2.
correspondences.note_en: Missouri considers financial resources and assets in maintenance proceedings and permits discovery of relevant documents. These texts do not establish a targeted judicial mechanism requiring the tax returns, expense records, or asset documents described in Article 1075-2.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque seules une pension alimentaire ou une contribution aux charges du mariage sont demandées, le juge doit inviter les parties à s’expliquer sur la prestation compensatoire avant de prononcer le divorce. Le Missouri règle la maintenance et les demandes de soutien, mais ne prévoit pas cette obligation procédurale spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: If only maintenance or contributions to marital expenses are sought, the French judge must invite submissions on a compensatory award before granting divorce. Missouri addresses maintenance and requested relief, but does not impose this specific invitation or compensatory-award procedure.

Braun v. Lied, 851 S.W.2d 93 (Mo. App W.D.).

(1993) Statute relating to parental support obligation does not require that child attend an institution of higher education on full-time basis. Age limitation protects parent from protracted college education. Harris v. Rattini, 855 S.W.2d 410 (Mo. App. E.D.).

(1993) Where child brought action against health care providers for injuries sustained during mother's pregnancy and child was not conceived at time of alleged negligent medical treatment, tort recovery was not barred by two-year statute of limitation. Exception to statute of limitations for children under age ten applied to action. Lough v. Rolla Women's Clinic, Inc., 866 S.W.2d 851 (Mo en banc).

(1994) Cadet at West Point was considered emancipated for purposes of child support even though academy provided education. Cadet's life at West Point is largely controlled by the government, which also provides for the bulk of the cadet's material needs. Federal law establishes that a cadet is part of the regular Army. Porath v. McVey, 884 S.W.2d 692 (Mo. App. S.D.).
(1997) Per diem payments received from an employer can be included in gross income when calculating a parent's child support obligation. Buckner v. Jordan, 952 S.W.2d 710 (Mo.banc).

(1997) Home-study program for attaining high school diploma was not "secondary school program of instruction" absent a showing of seriousness and good faith efforts on child's part to complete his education. Russell v. Russell, 949 S.W.2d 87 (Mo.App.W.D.).

(1999) Section requiring unmarried, divorced or legally separated parents to pay child support for college expenses does not violate equal protection clauses of federal and state constitutions. In re Marriage of Kohring, 999 S.W.2d 228 (Mo.banc).
(2000) Section requires child to receive credit for at least twelve hours to maintain eligibility to receive child support. Lombardo v. Lombardo, 35 S.W.3d 386 (Mo.App.W.D.).

(2004) Child's attention deficit hyperactivity disorder was manifest circumstance preventing successful completion of twelve credit hour requirement and thus continuing child support obligation. Pickens v. Brown, 147 S.W.3d 89 (Mo.App.W.D.).

norms.text:
1. Any person obligated under a judgment or order of a court to make installment payments of child support or spousal support may request from the person entitled to such support payments an affidavit attesting to the fact that the obligor is current in such support payments and that there are, on the date that the request is made, no installment payments due and unpaid. Upon such request by an obligor, any person entitled to child support or spousal support shall execute an affidavit as required by this section.

2. No affidavit shall be required to be executed if any installment of the obligor's support obligation is due or unpaid on the date that the request is made. If, however, any obligor who is current in payment of support obligations makes a request for a statement of that fact under this section and the person entitled to such support payment refuses or fails to execute the affidavit required by this section within ten days of the request, the obligor shall have a cause of action against such person for any damages caused by such failure or refusal and may, in addition to such cause of action, petition a court of competent jurisdiction to order the person entitled to the support obligation to execute the affidavit. Any person who executes a false affidavit under this section commits a class A misdemeanor as provided in section 575.050.

norms.heading: Support obligations, bond or other guarantee to secure, when required, procedure — default, effect of.

path.label: Title XXX DOMESTIC RELATIONS
Chapter 452 Dissolution of Marriage, Divorce, Alimony and Separate Maintenance

norms.text:
1. Upon entry of an order for support or division of property under this chapter or otherwise, or at any time the court finds any of the elements which constitute grounds for attachment under section 521.010, the court, by its own motion or that of a party or assignee of a party, may require that the obligor provide sufficient security, bond or other guarantee to secure the obligation to make support payments or to secure the division of property, conditioned that the obligor will pay all support payments as they come due, together with interest thereon, and will abide the orders of the court with respect to division of property.

2. The bond shall be filed with the clerk of the circuit court in the county where the order for support or division of property is filed, and the bond may be entered into before the clerk, if the court or judge entering the order for support or division of property shall first approve of the security.

3. The court, upon default in the condition of the bond, shall enter judgment against the obligors on the bond, according to the circumstances of the case, including interest or damages, and may award execution thereon, or otherwise enforce such judgment, according to the rules and practice of the court.

norms.heading: Maintenance or support payments to circuit clerk or family support payment center, when — procedure — duties of parties — failure to pay, circuit clerk duties.

path.label: Title XXX DOMESTIC RELATIONS
Chapter 452 Dissolution of Marriage, Divorce, Alimony and Separate Maintenance

norms.text:
1. As used in sections 452.345 to 452.350, the term "IV-D case" shall mean a case in which support rights have been assigned to the state of Missouri or where the family support division is providing support enforcement services pursuant to section 454.400.

2. At any time the court, upon its own motion, may, or upon the motion of either party shall, order that maintenance or support payments be made to the circuit clerk as trustee for remittance to the person entitled to receive the payments. The circuit clerk shall remit such support payments to the person entitled to receive the payments within three working days of receipt by the circuit clerk. Circuit clerks shall deposit all receipts no later than the next working day after receipt. Payment by a nonguaranteed negotiable financial instrument occurs when the instrument has cleared the depository institution and has been credited to the trust account. Effective October 1, 1999, at any time the court may upon its own motion, or shall upon the motion of either party, order that support payments as required by section 454.530 be made to the family support payment center established in section 454.530 as trustee for remittance to the person entitled to receive the payments. However, in no case shall the court order payments to be made to the payment center if the family support division notifies the court that such payments shall not be made to the center. In such cases, payments shall be made to the clerk as trustee until the division notifies the court that payments shall be directed to the payment center. Further, with the agreement of the division, the court may order payments to be made to the payment center prior to October 1, 1999.

3. The circuit clerk shall maintain records in the automated child support system which list the amount of payments, the date when payments are required to be made, and the names and addresses of the parties affected by the order. Nothing in this section shall prohibit the family support division from entering information in the records of the automated child support system, as provided for in chapter 454.

4. The parties affected by the order shall inform the circuit clerk or the payment center established in section 454.530 of any change of address or of other conditions that may affect the administration of the order.

5. For any case in which an order for support or maintenance was entered prior to January 1, 1994, which has not been modified subsequent to that date, except a IV-D case, if a party becomes delinquent in maintenance or support payments in an amount equal to one month's total support obligation, the provisions of this subsection shall apply. If the circuit clerk has been appointed trustee under subsection 2 of this section, or if the person entitled to receive the payments files with the clerk an affidavit stating the particulars of the obligor's noncompliance, the circuit clerk shall send by regular mail notice of the delinquency to the obligor. This notice shall advise the obligor of the delinquency, shall state the amount of the obligation, and shall advise that the obligor's income is subject to withholding for repayment of the delinquency and for payment of current support, as provided in section 452.350. For such cases, the circuit clerk shall, in addition to the notice to the obligor, send by regular mail a notice to the obligee. This notice shall state the amount of the delinquency and shall advise the obligee that income withholding, pursuant to section 452.350, is available for collection of support delinquencies and current support, and if the support order includes amounts for child support, that support enforcement services, pursuant to section 454.425, are available through the Missouri family support division of the department of social services.
revisor_notes: (1976) Proceeding to cite defendant for contempt for failure to pay court ordered support and maintenance for plaintiff and their minor children classified as civil contempt and subject to review on appeal. Judgment, with sentence of imprisonment, reversed and remanded since there was no evidence from which trial court could have concluded that defendant was financially able to pay the award. Teefey v. Teefey (Mo.), 533 S.W.2d 563.

(1976) Held that imprisonment for contempt is proper remedy for failure to comply with court order for maintenance and child support when person disobeying order has intentionally placed himself in a position which made compliance impossible. State ex rel. Stanhope v. Pratt overruling Coughlin v. Ehlert, 39 Mo. 285 (1866). State ex rel. Stanhope v. Pratt (Mo.), 533 S.W.2d 567.
(1976) Court may not amend an alimony payment order of its own motion. Dolan v. Dolan (A.), 540 S.W.2d 220.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise le versement des pensions alimentaires par intermédiation financière, sauf exclusion par les parents ou le juge. RSMo 452.345 permet ou impose le paiement au greffier ou au Family Support Payment Center, dont RSMo 454.530 précise le fonctionnement, mais dans un cadre institutionnel différent.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for financial intermediation of support payments unless excluded by the parents or judge. RSMo 452.345 permits or requires payment through the clerk or Family Support Payment Center, and RSMo 454.530 regulates that center, but under a different institutional framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1156 subroge le service de l’aide sociale à l’enfance, une œuvre ou un mandataire dans les droits du créancier pour recouvrer les subsides, et impose le reversement rapide des sommes à l’enfant ou à son représentant légal. Les textes du Missouri organisent l’assignation des droits de soutien, leur recouvrement et la redistribution des paiements, mais dans un cadre institutionnel et avec des délais différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1156 subrogates the child-welfare service, an organization, or a court-appointed agent to recover support and requires prompt payment to the child or legal representative. The Missouri provisions address assignment of support rights, collection, and payment distribution, but under different institutions and timing rules.
